transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-17
Time: 16:00 UTC (approx)
Duration: 47 mins
Attendees: Leah (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Arjun (CTO PineGrove), Maya (ML Eng), Jonas (Platform)

Auto-summary (brief):
Leah: quick intro and alignment on goals - reduce per-token cost for PineGrove's ingestion pipeline while maintaining inference fidelity for named-entity extraction and prompt-based summarization. Marco demoed the Optimize console: precision profiles, fidelity heatmaps, fallback rules between int8/fp8 and full fp16, and the sandbox runbook. Customer asked about worst-case rollback, KV cache behavior, and telemetry for quality drift. Agreed next steps: bench run, security pack, sandbox provisioning, and a pilot kickoff next week.

Topics covered:
- Quantization profiles: INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs
- Console tour: profile page, fidelity sampling, latency histogram, token-level cost
- Fallback policies and rollbacks
- Telemetry: sampling, signal thresholds, eval sets
- Edge-case behavior and hallucination risk
- Integration notes: API changes and dedicated/private options

Action items (as captured):
- Marco to run per-route sweeps and share results
- Leah to send contract/pricing and SOC2 docs
- Maya to provide prompts and sample testset

Transcript body:
[00:00] Leah: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um this is Leah from Redwood, i run the west AE team, quick intro from us, Marco's gonna drive today's console tour, priya's hanging to answer infra questions.
[00:14] Arjun: thanks, yeah appreciate it, i'm arjun, CTO at PineGrove. We're trying to get the cost down for our nightly ingest and also keep the NER accuracy; have some strict 99th latency SLAs for the web ui.
[00:28] Marco: cool, quick agenda, 1) show Optimize console profiles, 2) run an example int8 vs fp8 comparison with a small prompt set, 3) talk fallback rules and rollout plan. sound ok?
[00:40] Maya: yes sounds good, we have two critical routes, the realtime search autocomplete (tight latency) and a nightly summarization job (throughput but more tolerant).
[00:52] Marco: perfect, i'll pull up the sandbox. so this is the profile listing - you can see per-model profiles, and here we've pre-populated an int8 profile and an fp8 profile for your model family, note the quality baseline on the right - that's a delta against your eval set.
[01:18] Marco: hitting run on a small sample... ok results streaming, latency median is down ~22% on int8 but some outlier tails are worse, a few samples show hallucination-like truncation - that's expected for aggressively quantized weights, the console flags those as fidelity degradations.
[01:45] Arjun: when you say hallucination-like truncation, is that deterministic? is it a function of sequence length or the token distribution?
[01:58] Marco: good q. mostly sequence-length sensitive and also attention pattern variance; int8 is noisier for long seqs and for certain attentive slices. the KV cache behavior also matters - if you reuse cached prefixes the delta shrinks.
[02:20] Jonas: oh can we pin the warm-up cache? we have a warmed state for our nightly job where many prefixes repeat.
[02:27] Priya: yes you can set caching affinity in the runtime and Optimize will surface the expected improvement if prefix reuse > 30%.
[02:36] Maya: what's the telemetry story if fidelity drifts in production?
[02:41] Marco: console has sampling hooks - you can configure periodic draws to run the eval set with a blind holdout and have alerting when quality drops by X% (we saw you set X=2 in your doc). we also capture token-level probs to look for calibration shifts.
[03:02] Arjun: do we need dedicated machines to use int8 or can we do this on hosted?
[03:08] Leah: both. hosted supports int8 variants for many models; dedicated gives you more predictable tails and isolation if you want guaranteed latency SLOS. for PineGrove's 99th percentile we can discuss reserved capacity vs hosted burst.
[03:23] Maya: what about fp8? seems promising in some of the literature but vendor support varies.
[03:29] Marco: fp8 sits between int8 and fp16 - usually better fidelity than int8 with similar speedups on newer tensor cores, but it's more sensitive to kernel-level support. in our profiles fp8 often hits a nice latency-quality sweet spot, especially for summarization tasks.
[03:52] Arjun: can you show failure modes? i want to see rollback behavior if a precision profile spikes errors.
[03:58] Marco: yep. demoing fallback page - you can set a per-route rule: if fidelity metric (e.g., rouge/ent-F1) drops > 3% over rolling 1k samples, switch to the next higher precision and notify ops. if that doesn't recover, fall back to fp16 and open the incident.
[04:27] Marco: starting a simulated injection of corrupted prompts to push the metric. ok the policy triggered, saw a metric drop, next precision automatically engaged, latency rose slightly but error rate normalized. note the rollback log includes request ids and a stacktrace pointer so you can trace.
[04:49] Maya: are those request ids PII safe? we can't send raw user content to Redwood.
[04:55] Leah: by default logs are hashed and you can configure redaction. for Private we can host the telemetry collector in your VPC and only send aggregates to Redwood. we'll share the SOC2 pack and the telemetry schema.
[05:12] Arjun: ok good. also curious about mixed-workload behavior - our night job is long context, daytime is short. do you recommend separate routes or single model with adaptive profiles?
[05:22] Marco: recommend separate routes if you can, it's simplest. if not, Optimize supports per-request hints and runtime adaptive selection: route by latency budget header and select the profile that meets the budget. we've seen 10-15% better unit cost by splitting.
[05:39] Jonas: any changes to the API? we want minimal code changes.
[05:43] Priya: none required for simple rollouts - profile selection can be set server-side via routing policy. if you want client-control, it's an optional header.
[05:52] Maya: can we get the per-token cost breakdown?
[05:55] Marco: yep console shows token-level cost and aggregate, here's an example: nightly job cost drops ~40% with int8 but quality delta is 1.8% on your sample; fp8 drops cost ~28% with delta 0.6%.
[06:15] Arjun: the numbers look promising. what about worst-case latency tails on int8?
[06:20] Marco: we saw 99th bump by ~60ms in some synthetic batches; with dedicated capacity tails tighten. Also with batching policies you can reduce per-token cost with minor tail increases.
[06:34] Arjun: ok can we do a bench using our real prompts?
[06:37] Leah: absolutely, that's on the action items. Marco will run a 5k sample bench with your set.
[06:44] Maya: any guidance on eval metrics? we use F1 for NER and rouge for summarization.
[06:50] Marco: perfect combination. for NER pay attention to entity-level F1 and per-entity support frequency, for summarization check rouge-L and also human eval on a small blind set. console can plug in your eval harness.
[07:05] Arjun: what about binning by prompt length? some of our documents are 8k tokens.
[07:11] Marco: we support length buckets; optimize will show fidelity per bucket so you can see where int8 degrades. often int8 looks fine up to 2k but degrades beyond.
[07:25] Jonas: any talk about audit logs and who can see what in the console?
[07:29] Leah: RBAC is supported, SSO via SAML, and audit trails are stored per-account. for Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS/HSM.
[07:40] Arjun: security sounds fine, we'll need the SOC2 docs and the data residency notes.
[07:44] Leah: will share after call.
[07:48] Marco: one more nuance - some fp8 kernels can produce slightly different tokenization edgecases; we recommend running a tokenization diff as part of your sampling to catch those early.
[07:59] Maya: interesting, we saw weird token splits once in our pipeline with a new tokenizer update.
[08:05] Marco: console can run a tokenizer diff and flag anomalies.
[08:10] Arjun: ok can we discuss pricing briefly?
[08:13] Leah: high level - hosted per-token pricing with discounts for commit; dedicated has flat instance pricing and lower per-token. i'll send a tailored estimate.
[08:25] Maya: for the pilot we just need to validate fidelity on 2 routes, estimate cost and see operational playbooks.
[08:32] Marco: for pilot i'll run three profile sweeps (fp16, fp8, int8) and provide a table with latency med/99th, cost per million tokens, and fidelity deltas.
[08:45] Arjun: do you have a recommended rollback SLO?
[08:48] Marco: many customers use a 2-3% quality drop threshold on important metrics plus an ops notification and automated fallback. you can tune it.
[08:58] Jonas: curious if any competitors do better on tails; we mentioned Anthropic earlier, they have strong fp8 work but we need to verify integration effort.
[09:08] Leah: correct, competitor landscape varies; our differentiation is runtime-level fallback and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private.
[09:20] Maya: ok good. anything else?
[09:23] Leah: let's recap next steps.
[09:25] Marco: recap: Marco runs per-route bench and shares results; Leah sends pricing and SOC2; Priya provisions sandbox; Maya provides prompts.
[09:33] Arjun: thanks all. schedule follow-up for pilot kickoff next week.
[09:36] Leah: thanks everyone, we'll follow-up with calendar invite and links.

End of transcript.

Notes about transcription quirks: occasional speaker mislabels ("Speaker 4"), some run-on sentences, punctuation missing in places. Proper nouns sometimes fuzzy (fp16 vs f p sixteen), KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cache".
